meta.note: Every entry here was requested and its wording read in this session on 2026-11-20. Where a page could not be reached from this environment, that is stated rather than worked around.

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.used_for: Section 5, Identifying Yourself as an Associate — the required disclosure wording.
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Policies
sources.used_for: Participation Requirements §2(b): what Special Links must be, and the rule that price and availability may only appear when Amazon serves them or they arrive through Creators API / PA API.
sources.quote: Special Links enable accurate tracking, reporting, and accrual of commission income. Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you. … Because prices for and availability of Products that you have listed on your Site may change, your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License.

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
sources.used_for: Where an affiliate disclosure should sit, and what makes it clear and conspicuous.
sources.quote: if there’s a connection between an endorser and the marketer that a significant minority of consumers wouldn’t expect and it would affect how they evaluate the endorsement, that connection should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
sources.page_date: Up to date as of 2026-11-18 (88 FR 48102, July 26, 2023)
sources.used_for: The federal regulation (§§255.0–255.6, including §255.5 Disclosure of material connections) that the FTC FAQ interprets.
sources.quote: When there exists a connection between the endorser and the seller of the advertised product that might materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement, and that connection is not reasonably expected by the audience, such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.used_for: Confirms that rel="sponsored" is Google's documented marker for paid or advertising links, and that multiple rel values may be combined.
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

sources.title: Understanding ASINs: Your guide to Amazon’s product identification system
sources.used_for: Distinguish a listing identifier from a submitted short-link code.
sources.quote: It’s a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store.

sources.title: Performance report (Search results)
sources.used_for: Search performance queries, impressions and clicks.
sources.quote: The Performance report shows important metrics about how your site performs in Google Search results.

sources.title: Verify your site ownership
sources.quote: Ownership verification means proving to Search Console that you own a specific website.

sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.used_for: Official minimum safe internal cooking temperatures and rest times quoted in the thermometer pairing guide.
sources.quote: Beef, Pork, Veal, and Lamb (Steaks, Chops, Roasts): 145 °F (62.8 °C) and allow to rest for at least 3 minutes. Ground Meats: 160 °F (71.1 °C). All Poultry: 165 °F (73.9 °C). Fish & Shellfish: 145 °F (62.8 °C).

sources.title: Food Thermometers (Kitchen Thermometers)
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.used_for: Confirms that visual color cues are unreliable and that a food thermometer must be placed in the thickest part away from bone, fat or gristle.
sources.quote: Using a food thermometer is the only reliable way to ensure safety and to determine the 'doneness' of meat, poultry, and egg products.

sources.title: Catalog Items API v2022-04-01 Reference
sources.used_for: Documents Amazon's official Selling Partner catalog lookup endpoint (GET /catalog/2022-04-01/items/{asin}), distinct from Associates Creators API / PA API.
sources.quote: Retrieves details for an item in the Amazon catalog.
